name: Chapter 3: Balance Sheet — Liabilities and Equity — Mock-exam-calibrated MCQs (4–6 options)

questions.text: A security carries an unconditional contractual requirement to pay €8m in cash each year, despite being legally described as preferred shares. Under the lecture's IAS 32 decision logic it is:

options.a: a liability because the issuer has a contractual cash obligation.
options.b: an equity instrument because the contract states preferred dividends are cumulative rather than discretionary.
options.c: equity because preferred shares are legally named share capital.
options.d: equity because any fixed coupon is treated as an optional dividend.
options.e: an asset because the holder receives a contractual cash payment.
options.f: a liability only if the instrument has an observable secondary-market trading price above face value.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Current maturities of long-term debt are reported as current liabilities.
II. An issuer's obligation to deliver cash is a key debt-versus-equity criterion.
III. Liabilities are classified by the market price of a firm's common shares.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II only
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A supplier ships goods worth €12m on 60-day credit; the buyer records the inventory today and will pay later. The buyer's initial liability is most naturally:

options.a: a bank loan, reflecting the implicit discount on sales invoices.
options.b: trade accounts payable, reflecting financing from the supplier.
options.c: retained earnings, reflecting the inventory's increase in value.
options.d: A non-current liability, because goods purchased on credit do not create trade payables until the goods are sold onward.
options.e: deferred revenue, reflecting future performance obligations.

questions.text: An electronics retailer receives €2m for products it will deliver next quarter. How should the receipt generally be classified at the reporting date?

options.a: Cash increases and retained earnings directly increase by €2m.
options.b: Cash increases and an unearned-revenue liability is recognized.
options.c: The cash receipt is recognized as current-period sales revenue and as a liability until next quarter’s delivery.
options.d: Cash increases and accounts receivable is recognized for €2m.
options.e: The entity immediately recognizes net income while deferring the corresponding increase in cash.
options.f: Cash increases and current sales revenue is immediately recognized.

questions.text: A firm reports annual sales of €1,460m and average trade payables of €200m. Using the lecture's definition, its accounts-payable turnover and DPO are:

options.a: 7.75 and approximately 47 days
options.b: 6.30 and 58 days
options.c: 7.30 and 50 days
options.d: 6.85 and approximately 53 days

questions.text: A company's DPO lengthens from 42 to 75 days. Which combination is economically most plausible?

options.a: Supplier financing reduces cash, but late payments always improve credit ratings.
options.b: Supplier financing shortens collection periods, without affecting contractual terms.
options.c: Supplier financing temporarily supports cash, but delayed payments may harm relationships.
options.d: A higher DPO always proves improved supplier credit quality even if supplier invoices are overdue.
options.e: Supplier financing raises recognized revenue, while trade payables are unchanged.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Trade credit means purchasing goods or services before payment.
II. A higher DPO always proves stronger operational profitability.
III. An excessive DPO may be a symptom of liquidity pressure.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A manufacturing firm has DIO=82, DSO=47 and DPO=64 days. Its cash conversion cycle equals:

options.a: 71 days
options.b: 75 days
options.c: 129 days
options.d: 99 days

questions.text: A firm shortens DIO by 9 days, reduces DSO by 6 days and shortens DPO by 10 days. The resulting change in the cash conversion cycle is:

options.a: −25 days
options.b: −5 days
options.c: +5 days
options.d: +7 days

questions.text: A firm's working capital is €40m, based on €240m current assets and €200m current liabilities. It borrows €30m short-term and holds all proceeds as cash. What happens immediately?

options.a: NWC increases by €30m, while the current ratio rises to 1.35.
options.b: NWC rises to €70m, while the current ratio remains exactly 1.20.
options.c: NWC falls to €10m, while the current ratio increases to about 1.35.
options.d: NWC remains €40m, while the current ratio rises from 1.20 to 1.35.
options.e: NWC is unchanged, while the current ratio rises from 1.20 to 1.35.
options.f: NWC remains €40m, while the current ratio falls from 1.20 to about 1.17.

questions.text: A company reports current assets of €580m and current liabilities of €640m. Which interpretation is most defensible?

options.a: NWC is €60m; all near-term obligations are secured by excess current assets.
options.b: NWC is +€60m; the shortfall is eliminated because non-current liabilities are excluded.
options.c: NWC is −€60m; the firm must already be insolvent under every accounting standard.
options.d: NWC is €1,220m; inventory turnover becomes irrelevant for assessing liquidity.
options.e: NWC is −€60m; short-term funding demands warrant investigation, not automatic failure.
options.f: NWC of −€60m proves the balance sheet has negative equity and the company is already insolvent.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Unearned revenue reflects cash received before the promised delivery.
II. Both accrued expenses and unearned revenue necessarily arise from bank borrowing.
III. Accrued wages recognize services received but not yet paid for.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: I only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A company sells equipment with a two-year repair warranty. Historical experience makes repair costs reliably estimable. Which treatment best reflects the accrual concept?

options.a: Wait until every claim is physically repaired before recognizing any obligation.
options.b: Recognize a warranty expense and related liability when the sale creates the obligation.
options.c: Record the entire expected warranty cost as contributed capital on the sale date.
options.d: Recognize repair costs as new revenue because customers may claim later.
options.e: A warranty provision must be recorded as an inventory asset because its repair cost relates to goods sold.
options.f: The expense is recorded only when customers actually exercise their warranties and repair invoices are settled.

questions.text: An entity faces a lawsuit with a probable outflow that can be reliably estimated. Which conclusion is most consistent with accrual reporting?

options.a: Recognize a provision, with expense affecting the period's profit.
options.b: Defer recognition until the final settlement is paid in cash.
options.c: A probable outflow that can be estimated must be disclosed only; IAS 37 prohibits recognizing it as a provision.
options.d: Recognize a gain because litigation is not yet legally resolved.
options.e: A provision cannot be recorded until a court issues its final ruling, even if an outflow is probable.
options.f: Classify the estimated outflow as current operating cash inflow.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Bonds can trade after issuance in a secondary market.
II. A revolving credit line provides flexible borrowing up to an agreed limit.
III. A bondholder receives residual ownership rights identical to common shareholders.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: I and III only

questions.text: A fixed-rate bond is issued at par; market yields then increase sharply with no change in credit quality. The bond's secondary-market price will generally:

options.a: fall only if the issuer simultaneously reduces the coupon on old debt.
options.b: rise, because its contractual coupon automatically increases with yields.
options.c: remain at par, because a bond's issue price never changes afterward.
options.d: fall, because its fixed cash flows are discounted at a higher rate.

questions.text: An issuer has a 6% fixed-coupon bond outstanding. Its market price rises above par. Which market development is most consistent with this observation?

options.a: The issuer's retained earnings have necessarily become negative.
options.b: Contractual coupons on its outstanding bonds have increased automatically.
options.c: Required yields on otherwise similar bonds have risen above the coupon rate.
options.d: Required yields on otherwise similar bonds have fallen below the coupon rate.

questions.text: A firm's EBIT is €260m, gross interest expense €40m and net interest expense €25m. Using the lecture's formula, times interest earned is:

options.a: 7.50 times
options.b: 10.40 times
options.c: 5.85 times
options.d: 6.50 times

questions.text: A firm has CFO of €150m, short-term debt of €80m and long-term debt of €420m. Annual capital expenditure is €90m. Its adjusted CFO-to-total-debt ratio is:

Consider the statements.
I. Times interest earned directly includes all scheduled principal repayments.
II. Times interest earned compares EBIT to gross interest expense.
III. CFO-to-debt ratios assess debt-paying capacity from internally generated cash.
Which set is correct?

options.a: None of I, II or III
options.b: I and III only
options.c: II and III only
options.d: III only

questions.text: A profitable firm reports EBIT of €100m, interest of €20m and principal repayments of €150m. Why might a high times-interest-earned ratio give incomplete reassurance?

options.a: The ratio tests interest coverage but does not directly include scheduled principal repayments.
options.b: The ratio is calculated exclusively from changes in retained earnings and share issues.
options.c: The ratio is only defined when shareholders receive positive net payouts.
options.d: The ratio includes principal repayments but excludes contractual coupon payments.

questions.text: A parent controls 80% of a subsidiary and consolidates 100% of its net assets. The portion attributable to outside investors is shown as:

options.a: non-controlling interest within consolidated equity.
options.b: short-term debt because minority holders do not control operations.
options.c: The remaining 20% must be shown as a current liability because the parent does not control those shares.
options.d: an extraordinary gain recognized whenever profits increase.
options.e: goodwill because minority owners are not part of the group.
options.f: The remaining 20% is eliminated from the consolidated equity accounts because the parent controls most voting rights.

questions.text: Which calculation is most relevant to the return attributable to parent-company common shareholders?

options.a: Consolidated net income divided by average total assets including minority interests.
options.b: Parent-attributable profit divided by average common equity attributable to the parent.
options.c: Consolidated net income divided by average interest-bearing liabilities.
options.d: Total dividends paid divided by gross PPE after accumulated depreciation.

questions.text: A company reports common dividends of €2 per share, basic EPS of €8 and a stock price of €50. Which pair is correct?

options.a: Payout ratio 16%; dividend yield 10%
options.b: Payout ratio 25%; dividend yield 4%
options.c: Payout ratio 40%; dividend yield 2%
options.d: Payout ratio 4%; dividend yield 25%

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A secondary-market resale of existing shares automatically increases issuer equity.
II. Issuing common shares may increase contributed capital.
III. Retained earnings reflect cumulative profit not distributed.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: III only
options.d: I, II and III

questions.text: A company has €1.8bn book equity and 60m common shares. Its share price is €44. What are book value per share and market-to-book ratio?

options.a: €30 and about 1.50
options.b: €30 and about 1.47
options.c: €44 and about 0.68
options.d: €30 and about 0.68

questions.text: Two firms report identical book equity but very different market capitalizations. Which explanation is most consistent with the lecture?

options.a: Both market values are necessarily incorrect because shares trade only at reported book amounts.
options.b: A company's market value is determined entirely by its existing common-stock par value.
options.c: Book equity must equal market capitalization after normal financial statement consolidation.
options.d: Market values reflect expected future profitability and assets imperfectly captured by book values.

questions.text: A firm reports a positive change in cash but repeatedly delays payments to critical suppliers. What is the strongest analytical concern?

options.a: The cash improvement may be financed by stretching payables rather than operating strength.
options.b: The cash improvement proves that trade-credit terms have permanently improved.
options.c: Accounts payable are excluded from the cash conversion cycle and thus cannot matter.
options.d: The firm must have reported an equal positive change in its shareholders' equity.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Debt maturity concentration may create refinancing risk.
II. Current liabilities can include principal due on otherwise long-term borrowings.
III. Long-term borrowing eliminates the need to assess contractual interest payments.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I only
options.c: I and II only
options.d: I, II and III
options.f: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company reduces DPO while DIO and DSO are unchanged. What happens to the cash conversion cycle?

options.a: CCC remains unchanged, because payables do not enter the operating cycle.
options.b: CCC increases, because supplier credit covers fewer days of the operating cycle.
options.c: CCC becomes negative, because DPO must always exceed DIO and DSO.
options.d: CCC decreases, because supplier credit covers fewer days of the operating cycle.

questions.text: A business earns €50m net income, pays €15m in cash dividends, repurchases €10m shares and issues €20m shares. Its net payout and implication are:

options.a: −€5m net payout; the business raised slightly more than it distributed.
options.b: €5m net payout; the business distributed slightly more than it raised.
options.c: €45m net payout; the business distributed almost all its earnings.
options.d: €25m net payout; the business distributed all repurchase cash and dividends.

questions.text: A liquidity analysis compares firms with the same current ratio but materially different receivables quality. Why is the ratio alone insufficient?

options.a: Current ratios already adjust for all expected credit losses beyond reported allowances.
options.b: High-quality receivables are reported only in the non-current liabilities section.
options.c: Reported current assets may not be convertible to cash equally quickly or reliably.
options.d: A current ratio uses share market capitalization instead of short-term assets.

questions.text: A firm issues a 10-year bond to replace a revolving bank loan, with identical total borrowings. Which direct financing effect is most likely?

options.a: Its interest and principal commitments are extinguished rather than restructured.
options.b: Its operating revenue increases by the bond's full proceeds during the issue year.
options.c: Its debt disappears from the balance sheet because bonds are marketable securities.
options.d: Its maturity profile becomes longer, reducing immediate refinancing requirements.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Some securities labeled preferred shares may be classified as liabilities.
II. All preferred shares are common equity regardless of contractual settlement terms.
III. Preferred shares may have priority over ordinary shares for distributions.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: I and II only
options.c: III only
options.d: II only

questions.text: A retailer buys inventory on credit from a supplier and sells it to customers for immediate cash, before paying the supplier. Which operating characteristic may emerge?

options.a: A negative cash conversion cycle when supplier credit exceeds inventory and collection days.
options.b: Zero accounts payable because customer cash was received before the supplier's due date.
options.c: Higher days sales outstanding because all customer payments were collected immediately.
options.d: A necessarily positive cash conversion cycle whenever current assets exceed total liabilities.

questions.text: A firm extends DPO from 40 to 50 days, holds sales at €1,095m and uses the lecture's sales-based payable formula. Roughly how much supplier financing does this release?
Which change most directly improves the adjusted CFO-to-debt ratio while total debt and CFO remain constant?

options.a: Increasing capital expenditures, because they are added back to CFO.
options.b: Increasing gross interest expense, because interest is included in CFO.
options.c: Extending collection time, because receivables improve the ratio.
options.d: Reducing capital expenditures, although future operations might suffer.

questions.text: A company reports a jump in market-to-book value while book equity remains stable. Which conclusion is least warranted?

options.a: Market sentiment and required returns may have changed relative to the prior year.
options.b: Its net identifiable assets have necessarily been revalued upward on the balance sheet.
options.c: Investors may now anticipate higher profits or stronger future opportunities.
options.d: Intangible growth prospects not recognized in the accounts may contribute.

questions.text: A retailer records expenses in December for wages that will be paid in January. Which statement best describes the impact?

options.a: Current earnings increase and accrued liabilities fall, without December cash payment.
options.b: January sales decrease and current receivables rise, without December cash payment.
options.c: Current earnings are unaffected because expenses exist only when cash is transferred.
options.d: Current earnings fall and accrued liabilities rise, without December cash payment.

questions.text: Assume a share issue, a share repurchase, and dividends occur during the same year. Which item will normally decrease net payout to shareholders under the lecture definition?

options.a: Cash paid to redeem equity from owners
options.b: Cash spent buying back existing shares
options.c: Cash received from issuing new shares
options.d: Cash distributed as ordinary dividends

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. A contractual obligation to pay cash is an important indicator of a liability.
II. A share's legal label always determines its IFRS debt/equity classification.
III. Cash received for unfulfilled customer orders is immediately earned income.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: II only
options.c: None of I, II or III
options.d: I only

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Excessive supplier payment delays can damage relationships.
II. A longer DPO can release short-term cash.
III. Bond prices generally fall when required yields rise.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: II only
